content.title: About
content.content: Fried broccoli is broccoli quickly sautéed in a small amount of oil until it develops a golden crust. The cooking method retains most of the vitamins and minerals while giving the vegetable a crunchy texture and rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Broccoli belongs to the cruciferous family and is rich in glucosinolates, compounds with antioxidant properties.
Quick frying preserves more vitamin C than prolonged boiling.
Fried broccoli is a common side dish in Asian cuisine, often tossed with soy sauce and garlic.
A popular variation is "tempura broccoli," where florets are coated in batter before frying.
Broccoli is considered a "superfood" due to its high fiber and phytonutrient content.

items.title: High in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains vitamin K
items.content: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting and bone health.

items.title: Good source of fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and helps maintain satiety.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Phytonutrients such as sulforaphane help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium in broccoli contribute to normal blood pressure.

items.title: Cruciferous allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to broccoli.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Broccoli contains oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible people.

items.title: Added fat from frying
items.content: Using excessive oil can make the dish calorie‑dense.

items.title: Possible pesticide residues
items.content: Improperly washed broccoli may retain pesticide residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fried broccoli can be served as a side dish, tossed into salads, noodle or rice dishes. Season with soy sauce, lemon juice, garlic, or your favorite spices.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh broccoli in a sealed container in the refrigerator for 3–5 days. Cooked fried broccoli should be consumed within 1–2 days, kept refrigerated.
